title: Surjectivity of Word Selection
statement: Let $m$ and $u$ be binary words, with $|u|$ equal to the number of entries of $m$ that are $1$. There is a binary word $w$ of length $|m|$ whose selection along $m$ is exactly $u$.
hypotheses_covered: $|u|$ equals the number of $1$ entries of $m$
replaced: Let $m$ be a mask and let $u$ be a binary string whose length equals the number of $1$ entries of $m$. Then there is a choice word $w$ with $|w| = |m|$ whose selection along $m$ is exactly $u$.
